Inside the logs: projects, entries, checksums and the run log

pdmS7 documentation

Source: vignettes/log-structure.Rmd
log-structure.Rmd

pdmS7 keeps two kinds of log. A calibration log records how one model was calibrated: every decision, by whom, with which data and parameters, and why. A run log records every time a model is run, so any result can be traced to the parameters behind it. This article opens both up: what files they are, what is in them, and how they guard against being quietly changed. Logging a manual calibration shows how to use them; the design record explains why they are built this way.

A small project to look inside 

set.seed(1)
n <- 24 * 40
time <- seq(as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC"), by = 3600, length.out = n)
forcing <- data.frame(time = time, pet = 0.05,
                      rain = ifelse(stats::runif(n) < 0.07, stats::rgamma(n, 0.7, scale = 3), 0))
truth <- pdm_presets("standard")
truth$area_km2 <- 30
observed <- run_pdm(pdm_from_config(truth), forcing)$output$q_m3s
options(pdmS7.user = "Ann Hydrologist", pdmS7.role = "custodian")
project <- file.path(tempdir(), "inside")
start_calibration_project(project, catchment = "Example Brook", gauge = "99003",
                          purpose = "Illustration", area_km2 = 30,
                          owner = "Deputy Director", steward = "Sam Steward")
register_data(project, forcing, observed, calibration = c(121, 600),
              validation = c(601, 800), test = c(801, n))
start <- truth
start$fc <- 0.9
select_structure(project, start, "Standard PDM.")
log_trial(project, parent = 3, changes = c(fc = 1), verdict = "better",
          reasoning = "Volume was 10 per cent low.")
log_note(project, "Gauge checked against the station log.", refers_to = 2)
propose_candidate(project, entry = 4, reasoning = "Best so far.")
validate_candidate(project, "Holds on validation.")
test_candidate(project, "Holds on the final window.")

The project folder 

files <- list.files(project, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE)
files[!grepl("^report/", files)]
#>  [1] "data/0002/forcing.csv"               "data/0002/observed.csv"             
#>  [3] "entries/0001-project_start.yml"      "entries/0002-data_registered.yml"   
#>  [5] "entries/0003-structure_selected.yml" "entries/0004-trial.yml"             
#>  [7] "entries/0005-note.yml"               "entries/0006-candidate.yml"         
#>  [9] "entries/0007-validation.yml"         "entries/0008-test.yml"              
#> [11] "pdms7-project.yml"                   "series/0006.csv"                    
#> [13] "series/0007.csv"                     "series/0008.csv"
Path Holds
pdms7-project.yml Marks the folder as a project: format version and identifier
entries/ One YAML file per entry, numbered in the order written, never edited
data/0002/ Copies of the data registered by entry 0002, as CSV
series/ Full simulated and observed flow for candidate, validation and test entries
report/ The generated report, rebuilt on demand and never edited

Everything is plain text. A project can be read with any editor, kept on a shared drive or in git, and archived as it is.

An entry

Here is the trial, entry 0004, exactly as written:

cat(readLines(file.path(project, "entries", "0004-trial.yml")), sep = "\n")
#> # pdmS7 calibration log entry. Written once; never edit. verify_project() checks it.
#> format: 1
#> id: '0004'
#> type: trial
#> timestamp: '2026-11-01T18:39:36Z'
#> author:
#>   name: Ann Hydrologist
#>   role: custodian
#>   login: root
#> software:
#>   pdmS7: 0.3.1
#>   r: 4.3.3
#>   platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu
#>   engine: c
#> previous: 69b2cf77d13e35e0b5e1d856630d2c8a
#> registration: '0002'

#>   fc:

Every entry starts with the same header:

Field Content
format Entry format version
id Four-digit sequence number, as in the file name
type One of the eleven entry types
timestamp When it was written, UTC
author Declared name and role, and the operating-system login
software pdmS7 version, R version, platform and engine
previous Checksum (MD5) of the entry before it

The rest depends on the type. Numbers are written with the fewest digits that reproduce the exact value, so a configuration read back from the log is the configuration that ran.

The eleven entry types

Type Written by Role Key fields
project_start start_calibration_project() Custodian Catchment, gauge, purpose, area, Owner, Steward
data_registered register_data() Custodian Files and checksums, data quality, scoring windows, thresholds, headline
structure_selected select_structure() Custodian Configuration, scores, output checksum, reasoning
trial log_trial() Custodian Parent, changes, configuration, scores, output checksum, verdict, reasoning
auto_calibration log_auto_calibration(), compare_structures() Custodian Bounds, scales, method, objective, starts, every start’s result, configuration, scores
note log_note() Any Text and the entry it concerns
candidate propose_candidate() Custodian The run proposed, its scores, the saved series
validation validate_candidate() Custodian Validation scores beside calibration scores, saved series
test test_candidate() Custodian Test scores, scored once, saved series
sign_off sign_off_project() Steward or Delegated Steward Candidate, final configuration, checklist, statement
reopen reopen_project() Steward or Delegated Steward Reason

Trials, automatic calibrations and structures form a tree: every run names its parent, so the log records the path taken, dead ends included.

read_project(project)$entries[, .(id, type, author, summary)]
#>        id               type          author
#>    <char>             <char>          <char>
#> 1:   0001      project_start Ann Hydrologist
#> 2:   0002    data_registered Ann Hydrologist
#> 3:   0003 structure_selected Ann Hydrologist
#> 4:   0004              trial Ann Hydrologist
#> 5:   0005               note Ann Hydrologist
#> 6:   0006          candidate Ann Hydrologist
#> 7:   0007         validation Ann Hydrologist
#> 8:   0008               test Ann Hydrologist
#>                                   summary
#>                                    <char>
#> 1:           Example Brook - Illustration
#> 2:                               960 rows
#> 3:                          Standard PDM.
#> 4:                   fc 0.9 -> 1 (better)
#> 5: Gauge checked against the station log.
#> 6:                             Entry 0004
#> 7:                         Candidate 0006
#> 8:                  Candidate 0006 tested

The checksum chain

Each entry stores the checksum of the entry before it. Change one character of an earlier entry and its checksum changes, so the next entry’s previous no longer matches. Delete an entry, or slip one in, and the numbering or the chain breaks.

ids <- read_project(project)$entries$id
previous <- vapply(ids, function(i) read_entry(project, i)$previous, character(1))
k <- length(ids)
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
plot(NA, xlim = c(0.5, k + 0.5), ylim = c(0, 1), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
rect(seq_len(k) - 0.38, 0.35, seq_len(k) + 0.38, 0.75, col = "#eef4f6", border = pal[1])
text(seq_len(k), 0.62, ids, font = 2, cex = 0.85)
text(seq_len(k), 0.45, substr(previous, 1, 6), cex = 0.6, family = "mono", col = pal[5])
arrows(seq_len(k - 1) + 0.38, 0.55, seq_len(k - 1) + 0.62, 0.55, length = 0.06, col = pal[2])

Each entry’s ‘previous’ field holds the checksum of the entry before it (first six characters shown).

verify_project() walks the chain, checks every data and series file against its checksum and, with rerun = TRUE, repeats every run and compares the output checksum.

verify_project(project, rerun = TRUE)[, .N, by = .(check, ok)]
#>            check     ok     N
#>           <char> <lgcl> <int>
#> 1:     numbering   TRUE     8
#> 2:         chain   TRUE     8
#> 3:  data forcing   TRUE     1
#> 4: data observed   TRUE     1
#> 5:        series   TRUE     3
#> 6:         rerun   TRUE     4

Suppose someone tidies the reasoning of the trial after the event:

file <- file.path(project, "entries", "0004-trial.yml")
original <- readLines(file)
writeLines(sub("10 per cent", "8 per cent", original), file)
verify_project(project)[ok == FALSE]
#>     check  entry     ok                                      detail
#>    <char> <char> <lgcl>                                      <char>
#> 1:  chain   0005  FALSE Previous entry altered, removed or inserted
writeLines(original, file)

The edit to 0004 shows up at 0005, whose stored checksum no longer matches. Three details make the checks dependable in practice:

  • Line endings. Checksums ignore carriage returns, so a Windows checkout that converts line endings does not break the chain.
  • Output checksums are taken on flow rounded to 10 significant figures, so a project logged on one version of R verifies by rerun on another.
  • The newest entry has no successor to vouch for it. Sign-off, version control, or a managed drive covers it.

Writers take a lock on the project folder while appending, so two people working in one project on a shared drive cannot interleave entries.

The run log

The calibration log records how parameters were chosen; the run log records where they were used. It is off unless a path is set.

log_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "runs.csv")
register <- file.path(tempdir(), "approved.yml")
writeLines(c("projects:", paste0("  - ", basename(project))), register)

A register is a YAML file listing the projects whose signed-off configurations count as approved, with paths relative to the file:

cat(readLines(register), sep = "\n")
#> projects:
#>   - inside
options(pdmS7.run_log = log_file, pdmS7.register = register, pdmS7.run_tag = "example")
candidate <- read_entry(project, 6)$configuration
invisible(run_pdm(pdm_from_config(candidate), forcing[1:48, ]))
invisible(run_pdm(pdm_from_config(start), forcing[1:48, ]))
runs <- read_run_log(log_file)
names(runs)
#>  [1] "timestamp"   "user"        "login"       "tag"         "fingerprint"
#>  [6] "data_md5"    "rows"        "start"       "end"         "dt_hours"   
#> [11] "area_km2"    "engine"      "pdmS7"       "r"           "seconds"    
#> [16] "status"      "message"     "approval"    "project"     "sign_off"
runs[, .(tag, fingerprint = substr(fingerprint, 1, 8), rows, status, approval)]
#>        tag fingerprint  rows status   approval
#>     <char>      <char> <int> <char>     <char>
#> 1: example    a42af148    48     ok unapproved
#> 2: example    4df8c99c    48     ok unapproved
Column Content
timestamp, user, login, tag When, who, and an optional label from options(pdmS7.run_tag = )
fingerprint Checksum of the model’s components and parameters; see pdm_fingerprint()
data_md5, rows, start, end The forcing used
dt_hours, area_km2, engine, pdmS7, r Model and software
seconds, status, message Run time, and the error if it failed
approval, project, sign_off approved, superseded or unapproved, and the sign-off matched

Both runs show as unapproved: this project is validated and tested but not signed off. Once a Steward signs it off, runs with the candidate’s parameters are marked approved, with the project and sign-off entry; if the project is later reopened, they become superseded. Runs are never blocked.

The fingerprint recognises a model however it was built, from code, a preset or YAML, because it is taken on the model’s components and parameters, not on how they were written:

identical(pdm_fingerprint(candidate), pdm_fingerprint(pdm_from_config(candidate)))
#> [1] TRUE

Calibration evaluations, spin-up cycles and the calibration log’s own reruns are not logged, so the run log holds the runs people make. Logging is off by default, and a failure to write the log warns once and never stops a run.

Reading the logs

Function Returns
read_project() Project details, status and one row per entry
read_entry() One entry in full
project_trials() Every run with parent, changes, scores, verdict and reasoning
read_projects() One row per project, for a team folder or a large-sample batch
structure_comparison() A structure comparison’s ranking, rebuilt from the log
verify_project() The integrity checks
build_report() The report, as HTML and Markdown
read_run_log() The run log
approved_configurations() Every sign-off in a register, current or superseded
